text: Nhã Ca described the Battle of Huế in the documentary book Giai Khăn Sô cho Huế (Mourning Headband for Hue), published in Vietnamese in 1969. Although the book offered measured criticism of all three contending armies, it was freely published in Saigon and won a national literary prize. In Vietnam it was banned in 1975. The victorious communists publicly burned the book and in 1976 arrested Nhã Ca and her husband, fellow writer Trấn Dạ Từ, leaving their six children to fend for themselves. The ban is described as a response to the book's criticism of the actions of the national liberation front and its acknowledgement of the 1968 Huế massacre.
meta_description: Nhã Ca's Mourning Headband for Hue was banned in Vietnam in 1975; the book was burned and the author arrested in 1976.
changes: Chronological: 1969 publication, Saigon prize, 1975 ban, 1976 burning and arrests; ban reason from ban row.
